    com.im.njams.sdk.logmessage.Job.addActivity​(Activity)
    Use job.activities().add(activity) instead — obtain the facet via Job.activities() and call JobActivities.add(Activity). Unlike this method, the replacement does NOT require the job to be started: activities created before start are sent with the first log message after the job starts.
    com.im.njams.sdk.logmessage.Job.addAttribute​(String, String)
    Use job.attributes().add(name, value) instead — obtain the facet via Job.attributes() and call JobAttributes.add(String, String). Unlike this method, the replacement throws an exception when called after Job.end(boolean), because the final log message has already been sent and a later change is never sent.

    com.im.njams.sdk.logmessage.JobImpl.flush()
    SDK-internal flush mechanics, not part of the public API; there is no replacement — log messages are flushed transparently by the SDK because nJAMS server, respectively Elasticsearch, is not very good at handling high-frequency updates to the same job (logId). Do not call this method, and do not attempt to replicate it by sending messages through a sender instance directly.

    com.im.njams.sdk.Njams​(Path, String, String, String, ClientSettings)
    The runtime version is optional and therefore no longer a constructor parameter. Use Njams(Path, String, String, ClientSettings) and set the runtime version via njams.metadata().setRuntimeVersion(runtimeVersion) — obtain the facet via Njams.metadata() and call NjamsMetadata.setRuntimeVersion(String) before Njams.start(); NjamsMetadata.getRuntimeVersion() is the corresponding getter.

    com.im.njams.sdk.Njams.createProcess​(Path)
    Use njams.model().create(absoluteProcessPath) instead — obtain the facet via Njams.model() and call NjamsModel.create(Path).

    Behavior change: this legacy method treats its argument as a path relative to the client path and prepends the client path. The replacement NjamsModel.create(Path) expects the absolute process path (it must start with the client path) and does not prepend anything; build it with model().create(metadata().getClientPath().getOrCreateChild(...)) or use the single-segment convenience NjamsModel.create(String).

  • Interfaces 
    Interface Description
    com.im.njams.sdk.settings.SettingsProvider
    Use ClientSettings instead. Construct settings directly via the factory methods on ClientSettings (ClientSettings.from(java.util.Map), ClientSettings.from(java.util.Properties), ClientSettings.fromSystemProperties(java.util.function.Predicate)) or via ReadOnlyClientSettings.fromEnvironment(java.util.function.Predicate) for a read-only environment-backed view. The provider/factory layer is no longer needed.

    com.im.njams.sdk.common.Path
    Use Path instead, which guarantees path uniqueness, immutability, and thread-safety. Existing instances can be converted to the new type via Path.of(com.im.njams.sdk.common.Path).
    com.im.njams.sdk.model.layout.SimpleProcessModelLayouter
    Use CommonBfsModelLayouter instead. CommonBfsModelLayouter supports parallel branches, convergence, and nested groups correctly, and is the default layouter used by Njams since 6.0.
    com.im.njams.sdk.settings.provider.FileSettingsProvider
    Use ClientSettings instead. Load the file contents with the standard library (e.g. Properties.load(java.io.Reader) or Jackson) and pass the result to ClientSettings.from(java.util.Properties) or ClientSettings.from(java.util.Map). The provider/factory layer is no longer needed.
    com.im.njams.sdk.settings.provider.MemorySettingsProvider
    Use ClientSettings instead. Construct an in-memory settings view directly via ClientSettings.from(java.util.Map) (or ClientSettings.from(java.util.Properties)). The provider/factory layer is no longer needed.
    com.im.njams.sdk.settings.provider.PropertiesFileSettingsProvider
    Use ClientSettings instead. Load the .properties file with Properties.load(java.io.InputStream) and pass the result to ClientSettings.from(Properties). The provider/factory layer is no longer needed.
    com.im.njams.sdk.settings.provider.SystemPropertiesSettingsProvider
    Use ClientSettings.fromSystemProperties(java.util.function.Predicate) instead. The provider/factory layer is no longer needed.
    com.im.njams.sdk.settings.Settings
    This class is preserved only as a legacy implementation of ClientSettings for backwards compatibility with existing client code. The SDK itself no longer uses it internally — all internal settings handling now goes through the ClientSettings and ReadOnlyClientSettings interfaces. Obtain settings instances via one of the factory methods on those interfaces: ClientSettings.from(java.util.Map), ClientSettings.from(java.util.Properties), ClientSettings.fromSystemProperties(java.util.function.Predicate), or ReadOnlyClientSettings.fromEnvironment(java.util.function.Predicate) for a read-only environment-backed view.
    com.im.njams.sdk.settings.SettingsProviderFactory
    Use ClientSettings factory methods directly instead: ClientSettings.from(java.util.Map), ClientSettings.from(java.util.Properties), ClientSettings.fromSystemProperties(java.util.function.Predicate), or ReadOnlyClientSettings.fromEnvironment(java.util.function.Predicate) for a read-only environment-backed view. The provider/factory layer is no longer needed.

    Use njams.model().create(absoluteProcessPath) instead — obtain the facet via Njams.model() and call NjamsModel.create(Path).

    com.im.njams.sdk.Path.of​(Path)
    Switch callers from Path to the new Path type and construct instances directly via Path.of(String...) or Path.resolve(String...).
    com.im.njams.sdk.Path.toLegacyPath()

    com.im.njams.sdk.settings.encoding.Transformer.decode​(Properties)
    The ClientSettings interface decodes values on read via ReadOnlyClientSettings.getProperty(String). Callers that need a decoded Properties snapshot should use PropertyUtil.toProperties(com.im.njams.sdk.settings.ClientSettings) instead.
  • Constructors 
    Constructor Description
    com.im.njams.sdk.Njams​(Path, String, String, String, ClientSettings)
    The runtime version is optional and therefore no longer a constructor parameter. Use Njams(Path, String, String, ClientSettings) and set the runtime version via njams.metadata().setRuntimeVersion(runtimeVersion) — obtain the facet via Njams.metadata() and call NjamsMetadata.setRuntimeVersion(String) before Njams.start(); NjamsMetadata.getRuntimeVersion() is the corresponding getter.
